clue.text: A bad girl — one slipping into a loose blouse

indicators.note: one piece slipping into another sits inside it, so the letter for one goes into the jumble
loose means set free and disordered, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A naughty girl wriggles into a baggy top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like a description of the blouse, but it rearranges A BAD GIRL into GARBALDI; 'slipping into' then puts I after GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A garibaldi was a loose shirt for women, modelled on the red shirts worn by the Italian patriot's followers.

clue.text: Singular poet of importance

indicators.note: singular suggests removing the plural-looking final letter

parts.note: Robert Graves was an English poet

explanation.surface: An outstanding poet is said to be of real consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' turns GRAVES into a singular form by dropping its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave matters are serious and weighty.

clue.text: Was sick of beheading the unfortunate

indicators.note: beheading removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: the wretched are the unfortunate

explanation.surface: Someone was fed up with executing hapless people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was sick of' reads as being tired of; 'Was sick' is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Retched means heaved or vomited.

clue.text: Place in the park for players with Association experience

definitions.text: Place in the park for players

parts.note: a band is a group of people joined together
to stand something is to endure or experience it

explanation.surface: A park venue for footballers with Football Association experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Association' suggests football, but it is BAND, a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandstand is a covered platform in a park where musicians perform.

clue.text: Moan when Tom's first in handicapped race

parts.note: lame means disabled in the legs

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the phrase for handicapped race

parts.note: a nation is a people or race

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Tom

explanation.surface: Someone groans when Tom leads a handicap race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts T, from 'Tom's first', inside LAME NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamentation is a cry of grief or complaint.

clue.text: One member, a mischievous type …

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: One MP is a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a little devil, a naughty child.

clue.text: Reserved for a clown's replacement

indicators.note: replacement suggests the letters are put back in a new order

parts.note: a fool is a clown or jester

explanation.surface: Something is set aside for whoever stands in for a circus clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges A FOOL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person keeps to themselves, distant and standoffish.

clue.text: … concerned with love in a bar

indicators.note: in places the letter for love inside the word for bar

parts.note: but means except, as does bar
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: The troublemaker is preoccupied with romance in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it means except, BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: About means on the subject of, regarding.

clue.text: No capital, note, available for Japanese art

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
Riga is the capital of Latvia
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note says there is no money left for Japanese art.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Deliver weapon to a medieval mercenary

parts.note: to deliver is to set free
a lance is a long spear carried by knights

explanation.surface: Hand over a spear to a hired knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A free lance was a knight who sold his services to any lord who would pay.

clue.text: Frenchman comes before my return? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: one piece coming before another means it is placed first

parts.note: Anton is taken as a man's first name for a Frenchman

indicators.note: a return turns the word my back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman arrives ahead of my homecoming, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns MY into YM, which follows ANTON.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word of contrary meaning, such as hot against cold.

clue.text: Biographical sketch for the dossier

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
a dossier is a file of papers on a person

explanation.surface: A short life story is written up for a person's records.
explanation.definitionFit: A profile is a short written portrait of someone's life and character.

clue.text: The spirit of those parts

indicators.note: parts as a verb means splits up, so the word those is broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some regions have a distinctive local spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun meaning regions; it is a verb rearranging THOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a community.

clue.text: It sounds as if the horsy man has a spill in the twilight

indicators.note: these words say the answer is heard like the phrase that follows

parts.note: a horsy man is a knight on horseback, and a spill is a fall

explanation.surface: A rider tumbles from his horse as evening comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHT FALL, a mounted man falling, is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is the coming of dark at the end of the day, the time of dusk.

clue.text: Shopkeeper without experience whom Chesterton thought wicked

parts.note: someone green is new and untried
G. K. Chesterton's Song Against Grocers names the wicked grocer

explanation.surface: An untried trader was despised by the writer G. K. Chesterton.
explanation.walkthrough: G. K. Chesterton's poem begins 'God made the wicked Grocer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A greengrocer runs a shop selling fruit and vegetables.

clue.text: How to pay for fish

definitions.meaning: cash on delivery, abbreviated, is a way of paying when goods arrive
a common white sea fish of the North Atlantic

explanation.definitionFit: C.O.D. stands for cash on delivery, and the cod is a familiar food fish.

clue.text: Message for member thrust under taxi

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces beneath come after the taxi

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
a leg is a limb, a member of the body
to ram is to thrust or push hard

explanation.surface: A note for an MP who was shoved under a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts LEG and RAM below CAB in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cablegram is a telegram sent by undersea cable.

clue.text: Painter, a Medici perhaps, in a prison

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in tells us the jumbled letters go inside the word for prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of a Medici could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: An artist from the famous Florentine family, perhaps, is locked up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A MEDICI into ADEMICI, which 'in' puts inside CAN, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An academician is a member of an academy of art, such as a Royal Academy painter.

clue.text: National trial. I see, is disrupted

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A state trial is thrown into chaos, I notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun here, someone belonging to a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israelite is one of the ancient people of Israel, a member of that nation.

clue.text: Household head puts money on the first horse

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed before it

parts.note: bread is slang for money
the horse finishing first is the winner

explanation.surface: The head of the family bets the housekeeping on the favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts money on' reads as a bet, but BREAD goes in front of WINNER.
explanation.definitionFit: The breadwinner earns the income that supports a family.

clue.text: Blissful state destroyed by sect, say

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious group's happiness is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges SECT and SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is overwhelming joy or rapture.

clue.text: Expected precipitation, we were told

indicators.note: what we were told is what we heard, so the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: dew is moisture deposited from the air

explanation.surface: Rain was forecast, according to the weather report.
explanation.definitionFit: Something due is anticipated or scheduled to arrive.

clue.text: Accumulation is mounting in the warehouse

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for warehouse

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: mounting means rising, so in a down clue the word is is read upwards

explanation.surface: Stock is piling up in the storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns IS into SI, which 'in' puts inside DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a layer of material that has built up, such as silt.

clue.text: Novelist occupying the attention of a New Englander perhaps

indicators.note: occupying means filling, so the novelist's name sits inside the word for attention

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention
Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: A writer has the attention of someone from Massachusetts or Maine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts STERNE inside EAR. New Englanders live in the north-eastern United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the eastern seaboard of the United States, New England among it, is called that.

clue.text: Go in for record

definitions.meaning: to write down in a register or ledger

explanation.definitionFit: To enter is both to step inside and to note an item in a book.

clue.text: Exhibitions by former airmen

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
POs are pilot officers, airmen of the RAF

explanation.surface: Displays are staged by veterans of the air force.
explanation.definitionFit: Expos are large public shows or trade fairs.

clue.text: This boy's said to be bright

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: sunny means bright and cheerful

explanation.surface: Someone claims this lad is clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bright' looks like clever, but it is SUNNY, as in weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonny is a familiar way of addressing a young lad.

clue.text: See the parson about a source of power

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for parson goes round the letter A

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: Go and consult the vicar about where to find energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only an instruction; 'about' puts RECTOR around the A that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is a plant generating energy from atomic fission.

clue.text: Romany gentleman's drink

definitions.meaning: in the Romany language, a ... is a gentleman, as in George Borrow's Romany ...

explanation.definitionFit: Borrow's novel Romany Rye uses the Gypsy word for a gent, and the grain gives a whiskey.

clue.text: Told to put container on camel

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the phrase is identified by how it is heard

parts.note: a case is a container, followed by the word on

explanation.surface: Someone was instructed to load a box on to a dromedary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camel' is not the animal: it is a watertight float used to raise ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A camel in engineering is a buoyant watertight chamber, the same device as a caisson.

clue.text: Dignitary's steed, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: a mare is a female horse, so a steed

explanation.surface: This is the horse belonging to a civic official.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayor is the elected head of a town council, a civic figure.

clue.text: Win free-style in a determined way

parts.note: to earn is to win, as in winning a reward

indicators.note: free means released from order, so the letters of style are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer resolves to take the freestyle race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges STYLE into ESTLY, after EARN.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means seriously and with resolve.
